anchor.quote: Fix a positive integer $\beta$, the number of places, and positive integers $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_\beta$.
Here $\lambda_j$ is the length of place $j$, the number of values the digit at place $j$ can take.
The place index $j$ runs from $1$ to $\beta$ and names a place.
Let $\Lambda = \lambda_1\lambda_2\cdots\lambda_\beta$ be the product of the lengths, the number of distinct digit strings the system can write.
The place value of place $j$ is $w_j = \lambda_1\lambda_2\cdots\lambda_{j-1}$, the product of the lengths of the places below it, with $w_1 = 1$.
Let $\nu$ be an integer with $0 \le \nu < \Lambda$, the integer being written.
The digit $e_j$ at place $j$ is an integer with $0 \le e_j < \lambda_j$, the digit of the expansion at that place.
where $e'_j$ is the digit at place $j$ of the second expansion
Here $i$ is a place index that runs over the places below $j$.
every length is $b$ it is the base-$b$ expansion
anchor.note: The example first uses b as a common length and base, with no sentence saying what b denotes. The only earlier binding of b (on the logarithm page) is a different quantity, the base of a logarithm.

gaps.note: The place-value definition w_j and the telescoping identity are stated only for places j from 1 to beta. The page applies them at j = beta+1 without saying that the same formula defines w_{beta+1}, so the reader cannot check that the sum telescopes to Lambda - 1 from what the page gives.
